images.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: a premium, wide landscape hand-drawn concept board for a public developer README.
Primary request: show a responsible long-term memory loop for a glasses sports coach. This is a design concept, not a deployed product or real session.
Scene/backdrop: clean warm-white paper fills the ENTIRE canvas; very subtle paper grain only; flat illustration, not a photograph.
Style: imperfect black gel-pen doodles, a few cross-hatched surfaces, large royal-blue handwritten English labels and blue arrows, very sparse mustard-yellow accent lines; generous internal whitespace. Consistent with a friendly technical notebook. Landscape about 2:1.
Composition: one readable left-to-right main route across the upper two-thirds, with a consent-controlled write branch underneath. Six core nodes, simple silhouettes of a speech bubble and runner, memory notebook, coach conversation, consent diamond, saved entry and a receipt slip. No complicated UI.
Required exact labels, verbatim, and arrow relationships:
Title at top: "A coach that remembers"
Small subtitle: "DESIGN CONCEPT"
Main chain: "Current conversation / workout" -> "Recall only when needed" -> "Context-aware coaching".
Under the recall notebook, short blue labels: "Preferences" ; "Goals" ; "History".
From "Context-aware coaching" a clearly directed downward arrow goes to a small decision diamond labeled "Save permission?".
The decision has two distinct branches: an arrow labeled "Yes" goes right to "Save permitted context"; an arrow labeled "No" goes left to "Continue without saving".
From "Save permitted context" draw an arrow to a small receipt labeled "Accepted". Below it render the exact note "Accepted != searchable".
A dotted arrow labeled "Verify recall later" returns from the saved context/receipt area to the recall notebook.
Important semantics: answer first with bounded relevant context, and save ONLY after permission. The diagram must not imply all previous history is always fetched or that an accepted write guarantees searchable extracted memory. The no branch has no cloud or write. Do not add measured accuracy, speed, health numbers, user data or fabricated evidence.
Text should be large, sparse and hand-written, no paragraphs. All quoted words spelled exactly. No logos, brand marks or watermarks. All visual content comfortably inside canvas, no cropped labels.
Strict background constraints: NO desk, NO tabletop, NO dark outer border/frame, NO visible sheet edges/corners or curled paper, NO photographic cast shadows, NO overhead-photo staging, NO gradient, NO photorealistic effects. White/warm-white reaches all four image edges. Do not show a physical sheet sitting on something. Avoid polished vector boxes. Draw clean charming black-pen icons and royal-blue labels only, with sparse yellow.

images.initial_prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: a wide landscape hand-drawn developer journey illustration for a public README, reusable across Chinese, English and Japanese guides.
Scene/backdrop: clean full-bleed warm-white paper with only very subtle grain. Flat illustration, NOT a photo. White extends to all four edges. No visible paper boundary.
Style/medium: charming imperfect black gel-pen doodles, occasional cross-hatching, large royal-blue hand-written English labels and blue arrows, very sparse mustard-yellow accents; clean generous whitespace. Wide landscape around 2:1.
Primary request: accurately show developers two separate ways to add memory to Rokid glasses software. It is a development route concept, not a claim of an already deployed integration. Five major stages arranged horizontally left to right, with a clear vertically separated pair of alternative branches at the second stage, merging into common engineering stages.
Exact title at top: "Build a memory-aware glasses app".
Small subtitle under title: "DEVELOPER JOURNEY".
Flow:
First node far left: a simple sketch of generic glasses with a question mark, label "Choose your runtime".
A blue arrow forks into two DISTINCT independent route lanes in the next area:
upper lane has a tiny code/module doodle and exact label "AIUI JS SDK", connected by a short arrow to "EverOS";
lower lane has a tiny glasses-app doodle and exact label "Rokid SDK app", connected by a short arrow to "EverMe".
Do not draw an arrow between these two alternative lanes. They are choices, not a sequence. Add exact small note between/below lanes: "Choose one route".
Each lane independently converges to next stage, a padlock + server doodle labeled "Identity + service setup". This means developer setup after selecting the route; it is not a raw network topology and must not imply the SDK bypasses application authentication.
Then a solid arrow to a terminal/test checklist doodle labeled "Local checks".
Then a DOTTED arrow to far-right glasses+cloud outline labeled "Live service + glasses". This final stage is clearly pending, not a green success: use an empty checkbox or dashed open circle, tiny yellow flag, and exact label "Validation pending".
Small final caption at bottom: "Local tests != device acceptance".
All runtime words verbatim and exact. Never call the Rokid route an APK relay. Do not add a phone or show a mandatory smartphone relay. Do not depict Skill as a runtime component, do not draw SDK calling Skill, and do not conflate EverOS and EverMe. Do not invent performance numbers or real deployment claims.
All labels sparse and legible, hand-written rather than typeset. Keep all content safely inside canvas with broad margins.
Strict avoidance: NO logos or brand marks, NO watermarks, NO desk/tabletop, NO dark borders or outer frame, NO visible paper edges or curled corners, NO photographic cast shadows, NO overhead-photo staging, NO gradient or polished vector cards. Only black doodles, royal-blue handwriting, sparse yellow on warm white.
